title: Backup & Disaster Recovery
description: Plan and rehearse the recovery of an IT environment after failure. Tests 3-2-1 backup design, tabletop DR exercises, and business continuity tiering.

seo.overviewBody: Data loss or ransomware attacks can disrupt business operations permanently without robust backups. System engineers prove competence by establishing Recovery Time Objectives (RTO), Recovery Point Objectives (RPO), 3-2-1 backup strategies, immutable cloud storage, and DR failover drills.

deliverables.title: 1. Disaster Recovery & Business Continuity Plan
deliverables.desc: Comprehensive DR strategy documenting RTO/RPO metrics, backup retention windows, and emergency failover protocols.

deliverables.title: 2. Automated Backup & Cloud Sync Script
deliverables.desc: Script executing automated database and file snapshots with encrypted offsite cloud synchronization.

deliverables.title: 3. DR Failover Drill Verification Report
deliverables.desc: Audit log documenting a simulated server crash, backup restoration, and database integrity validation.

faqs.question: What is the 3-2-1 backup strategy?
faqs.answer: Keep 3 copies of your data on 2 different media types, with at least 1 copy stored in an offsite or cloud location.

faqs.question: What is the difference between RTO and RPO?
faqs.answer: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is the maximum acceptable duration of downtime. Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time.

faqs.question: Why is immutable backup storage essential against ransomware?
faqs.answer: Immutable backups cannot be modified, encrypted, or deleted by unauthorized software or ransomware attackers after creation.
